notes.meaning: We are warned not to be jealous of evil people or wish to spend time in their company. Even when sinners seem successful or happy, their path is harmful and leads to destruction. Do not let yourself be drawn into their lifestyle.

Evil people spend their time planning violence and using their words to stir up trouble. They plot ways to cheat or harm others, yet their schemes often bounce back on their own heads. Stay away from people who delight in tearing others down.
A home and a family are built up through wisdom and made secure through good understanding. True stability comes from living in God's ways rather than by cheating or hurting others to get ahead.

Knowledge fills every room of a home with precious and pleasant treasures. This includes practical goods earned through honest labor, but even more it means spiritual gifts like peace, love, and knowing God.
A wise person has real strength, and growing in knowledge adds power to one's life. Good sense and trusting God can accomplish far more than brute physical force ever could.
Great struggles and conflicts require careful thought and wise direction. Real victory and safety come when a person listens to many trusted counselors rather than relying only on oneself.

Wisdom seems far out of reach to a fool because he will not put in the work or turn from sin to learn. When the community gathers at the city gate to make important decisions, he has nothing helpful to offer and stays silent.

Anyone who sits around planning evil deeds will soon earn the reputation of being a schemer. Even if a person tries to mask his bad plans with smooth talk, people will eventually see his corrupt heart.
Even the inner thoughts and schemes of folly are sinful before God. A mocker who scoffs at truth and rejects correction ends up detested by everyone around him.
Giving up when hard times arrive shows how small your strength really was all along. Hardships test our faith and reveal whether our inner courage is genuine.

God commands us to step in and rescue people who are being led away unjustly to death or slaughter. If innocent people are in danger of violence or unfair treatment, we must do whatever we can to protect them.

Claiming that we did not know someone was in danger will not excuse our inaction. God sees deep into every heart, knows our real motives, and will hold us accountable for turning a blind eye to others in need.
Honey is sweet, nourishing, and good to eat fresh from the honeycomb. The teacher points to this sweet natural food to set up a picture of how wonderful wisdom is.
Just as honey tastes good to the tongue, godly wisdom brings deep joy and health to the soul. If you find and keep this wisdom, you will have a secure future and a hope that will never be cut off.
Wicked schemers are warned not to ambush the righteous person or try to tear down his home. Plotting against a godly person's resting place will fail because the Lord guards him.
Even if a righteous person falls many times into trouble and suffering, God raises him back up. The wicked, on the other hand, have no divine help and collapse completely when disaster strikes them.

differ.view: The verse refers strictly to falling into outward troubles and suffering, and should not be used to teach that believers can never fall away from grace.
The verse includes believers falling into sins, showing that God will restore them through repentance and preserve them from ever falling away completely.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Preachers historically applied this passage to moral weaknesses, teaching that a righteous person might fall into venial (lesser) sins multiple times a day while still remaining in God's love.

notes.meaning: We are told never to celebrate or feel happy inside when an enemy trips and falls into ruin. Taking personal delight in someone else's pain goes against God's call to love our enemies.
If you gloat over an enemy's disaster, the Lord notices your spiteful attitude and will be displeased. He may even take His anger away from your enemy and discipline you instead.
Do not burn with anger or become upset over wicked people, and do not envy their apparent success. Fretting over their short-lived advantages only robs you of your own peace.
Wicked people have no lasting future, and their lamp of prosperity will eventually be snuffed out. Their good fortune ends with this life, leaving them with no eternal hope.
We are called to honor both the Lord and the king, putting our fear of God above all else. Avoid joining with restless, rebellious people who try to overturn lawful authority.
Disaster will strike rebels quickly and without warning. No one can foresee how terrible the punishment will be when both God and the ruler act to crush rebellion.
A fresh collection of wise teachings begins here, especially for judges and community leaders. Showing favoritism in legal decisions is completely wrong because justice must always be fair.
Any judge who lets a guilty person off by calling him innocent will be cursed by the public. When justice is twisted, entire nations feel the harm and rightly express their outrage.
Judges who have the courage to convict and punish the guilty will find peace and respect. Rich blessings from God and gratitude from the people rest on those who uphold justice.
Giving a direct, truthful answer is as pleasant and welcome as a kiss on the lips. People deeply respect someone who speaks plainly and honestly instead of telling flattering lies.
A wise worker prepares his outdoor chores and plants his crops before spending money to build a home. You should secure a steady source of food and income before focusing on comfort and luxuries.
Do not volunteer to speak against a neighbor without a clear, necessary reason, and never tell lies about him. It is wrong to spread damaging stories simply out of spite or gossip.
Never seek revenge by promising to pay someone back for the wrong he did to you. True justice belongs to God, so we must leave vengeance in His hands rather than trying to get even.
The teacher describes walking past the field and vineyard of a lazy person who lacked good judgment. Looking at neglected land shows what happens when someone refuses to take responsibility.

The entire field was overgrown with thorns, nettles covered the soil, and the protective stone wall had crumbled away. Without steady care and hard work, even productive land quickly falls into complete ruin.
The teacher carefully examined the ruined vineyard and took an important lesson to heart. Wise people learn valuable truths by observing the mistakes and failures of others.

The lazy worker always asks for just a little more sleep, another nap, and a brief moment to rest his hands. Making small excuses to avoid daily work quickly turns into a destructive habit of idleness.
Because work was constantly put off, poverty suddenly ambushes the lazy person like a robber on the road. Desperate need overpowers him with unstoppable force, leaving him ruined.
